tool: Antigravity CLI (agy) 1.5.15 in print mode, run in an empty directory outside the repository: `agy -p "<request>" --model gemini-4-neon-high --mode accept-edits --sandbox --output-format json`. The agent hands the request to its built-in image-generator subagent, which writes the image prompt and calls its generate_image tool.
model: gemini-3.1-flash-image behind generate_image (the service named it in a capacity error of the same session; the tool does not report it on success); agent gemini-4-neon-high; image-generator subagent gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high.
prompt: Photorealistic seamless tileable surface texture of light neutral grey moulded matte plastic with a fine spark-eroded micro-stippled grain. Viewed strictly straight-on top-down orthographic macro view, completely flat and even diffuse illumination across the entire 1:1 square frame. Uniform fine matte stipple detail edge to edge for 3D material tiling, neutral very light grey tone, soft even surface without shadows, highlights, vignetting, perspective, objects, or text.
request: Generate exactly one image with aspect ratio 1:1 and nothing else. Image description: A seamless tileable surface texture of moulded plastic with a fine matte spark-eroded grain, a very light, near-neutral grey colour, even fine stippling, viewed perfectly straight on (orthographic, top-down), completely flat even diffuse lighting, no shadows, no specular highlights, no vignetting, no perspective, no objects, no text, no logos, no markings, uniform detail across the whole frame so it can tile seamlessly in a 3D material, photorealistic, square.
postProcessing: 1. ImageMagick 7.1.2-36, a one-off conversion of the generated JPEG to an 8-bit RGB PNG: `magick source.jpg -strip -colorspace sRGB -type TrueColor PNG24:source.png`. 2. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts prepare plastic source.png`: the last 128 columns and rows are cross-faded into the first ones (seamless, 896x896), the broad light and shade is removed (a wrapping box blur of radius 112 subtracted, the mean kept), and the image is area-averaged to 512x512, converted to grey (Rec. 709 luminance) with its mean moved to 224 of 255 so the renderer tint sets the colour. 3. `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` writes normal.png, roughness.png and metalness.png from basecolor.png. 4. 2026-11-24, after the owner's review of the pilot (the surface looked pitted at close range): the recipe of this material in tools/plant/textures.ts became heightBlur 3, normalStrength 0.08, roughness 0.95 to 0.88 (it was heightBlur 1, normalStrength 0.5, roughness 0.6 to 0.45), for a smooth, satin surface, and `bun tools/plant/textures.ts derive` wrote normal.png and roughness.png again; basecolor.png and metalness.png did not change. The roughness map is now a narrow band near 1 that the renderer's roughness of each surface scales.
